papers.title: On the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in spaces generated by Rademacher functions and their $p$-adic analogues
papers.abstract: Sufficient conditions for the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in the space spanned by generalized Rademacher functions are proved. It is shown that the sufficient number of nodes for discretization with the minimal number of nodes is equal to $N$ or $N+1$ and depends on the dimension $N$. The conjecture of F.~Dai, A.~Prymak, V.~N.~Temlyakov, and S.~Yu.~Tikhonov on the positivity of weights in the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm with a minimal number of points considered. It was investigated in which cases it holds and in which it fails for the spaces spanned by the $N$ generalized Rademacher functions with base $p$, and how the validity of the conjecture in this case depends on the parameters $p$ and $N$. The connection with generalized Hadamard matrices, the Hadamard's conjecture and Seberry's conjecture is demonstrated.

papers.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
papers.abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^\beta$ Poincar\'e inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $\lambda(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-\beta}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.

papers.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
papers.abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].

papers.title: Interpolation of nonlocal Sobolev spaces for general gradients
papers.abstract: We study the interpolation structure of nonlocal Sobolev spaces associated with general radial gradients. For compactly supported kernels satisfying suitable regularity and two-sided growth assumptions of fractional order, we characterize the spaces $H^{\rho,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $1<p<\infty$, by the Gustavsson--Peetre interpolation method between $L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The function parameter is determined, up to equivalence, by the behavior of the kernel near the origin. We also establish a complex interpolation formula between spaces associated with different kernels and integrability exponents, in which the interpolated kernel is their geometric mean. For the corresponding nonlocal Gagliardo spaces $W^{\rho,p}(\R^n)$, defined through an integral seminorm of first differences, we prove an identification with generalized Besov spaces and a real interpolation characterization involving the same function parameter. These results extend the classical relation between Bessel potential and Gagliardo spaces beyond power-type kernels, yielding continuous embeddings between the two families and their coincidence in the Hilbertian case. We further discuss logarithmic kernels and restriction spaces on Lipschitz domains, and obtain extension and compact embedding results for the Gagliardo spaces under weaker assumptions on the kernel.

papers.title: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
papers.abstract: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.

papers.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
papers.abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

papers.title: Multiplicities and $k$-numerical Range
papers.abstract: We study the wedge and projection multiplicities of a point in the $k$-numerical range $W_k(A)$ of a complex matrix $A$. The representatives are decomposable wedges of orthonormal $k$-frames and rank-$k$ orthogonal projections, respectively. For $1\le k<n$, put $r=\text{dim}_\mathbb{R}\text{span}_\mathbb{R}\{I_n,H,K\}$, where $H=(A+A^*)/2$ and $K=(A-A^*)/(2i)$. We prove that every $\xi\in\text{relint} W_k(A)$ satisfies $p_{A,k}(\xi)=n^2-r+1$ and $w_{A,k}(\xi)=\binom nk$. We determine both multiplicities at every boundary point of $W_k(A)$, including non-exposed points. For complex symmetric matrices we establish lower bounds for both real multiplicities, including singular interior fibers, and obtain exact formulas for boundary points, line ranges, and commuting symmetric parts. We also relate the two multiplicities by quadratic inequalities.

papers.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
papers.abstract: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $\tau$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,\tau}-(F,S(\tau)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.

papers.title: Two-Sided Weighted-History Transfer for Abstract Systems with Infinite Memory
papers.abstract: We prove a two-sided transfer principle for second-order systems with Hilbert-valued infinite memory. The squared norm of the coupled semigroup, from a centered weighted-history space into the energy space, is bounded above and below by constant multiples of $\rho_w(t)$. Here $\rho_w(t)$ is the squared norm of the right-translation semigroup between the corresponding weighted and unweighted memory spaces. The coupled system satisfies an energy identity, a mechanical multiplier estimate and a bounded observation. The memory density has decay of order at most polynomial, and the weight is admissible. Under these hypotheses the energy is bounded by the initial norm times $\kappa(t)+\rho_w(t)$, where $\kappa$ is the tail of the kernel. The two-sided equivalence holds when $\rho_w$ is integrable and the kernel has a finite first moment and satisfies a tail bound, or when $\kappa\le C_\kappa\rho_w$. For the density $pb(1+s)^{-p-1}$, with $p>1$ and $b>0$, and the weight $(1+s)^{2\theta}$, with $\theta>0$, the rate is $(1+t)^{-\min\{2\theta,p+1\}}$. For kernels and weights with logarithmic factors, under explicit conditions on the exponents, the logarithm of the weight enters the rate below the saturation threshold, and the logarithm of the kernel enters above it. A theorem with a prescribed decay of the inherited history gives exact exponents for algebraically growing histories. The hypotheses are verified for gradient-memory waves without instantaneous damping, endpoint-damped strings, damped plates and oscillators.

papers.title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
papers.abstract: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{\alpha,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{\alpha,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.

papers.title: Weighted Inequalities for the Fractional Maximal Operator on Trees with Flow Measures
papers.abstract: This paper develops a weighted theory for the fractional Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M_{\mu,\gamma}$, $0<\gamma<1$, on infinite trees equipped with flow measures. Such measures are typically nondoubling and exhibit exponential volume growth, so the classical Muckenhoupt theory does not apply directly. By replacing Euclidean balls with admissible trapezoids, a class of fractional $A(p,q)(\mu)$ weights is introduced, and a Muckenhoupt-type theorem is established: for $1\le p<1/\gamma$ and $1/p-1/q=\gamma$, the operator $M_{\mu,\gamma}$ is bounded from $\ell^p_\mu(\omega^p)$ to $\ell^q_\mu(\omega^q)$ if and only if $\omega\in A(p,q)(\mu)$. The endpoint case $p=1$ is characterized via a weak-type estimate.

papers.title: Fractional Triangular Maximal Operators on Locally Finite Trees
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the centered and uncentered fractional triangular maximal operators, $\mathcal{N}^\gamma$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^\gamma$, on locally finite trees. A key geometric tool that consists of a family of overlapping triangles with total measure comparable to a ball is established, which facilitates the analysis of ball-type maximal operators. Our main results include: complete pointwise comparisons among these and classical fractional maximal operators on homogeneous trees; sufficient geometric conditions and counterexamples for general trees; and sharp $\ell^p \to \ell^q$ boundedness theorems for the new maximal operators, with optimal ranges of exponents verified by counterexamples. Finally, we compare the unboundedness regions of the ball-type maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}^\gamma$ and the triangular maximal operator $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^\gamma$ on a prototypical tree, proving that the former's region strictly contains the latter's for all $0 < \gamma \leq 1$.

papers.title: Sharp Poincar\'e-Wirtinger Inequalities on Finite Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G_n=(V_{G_n},E_{G_n})$ be the finite connected graph with $n\geq3$ vertices. We study the sharp constant $C_{G_n,p}$ such that the Poincar\'{e}-Wirtinger inequality \[ \Vert f-m_f\Vert_p\leq C_{G_n,p} {\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}(f) \] holds for every $f$ on $V$, where ${\rm Var}_{p}^{G_n}$ stands for the $p$-variation on $G_n$ and $m_f$ stands for the arithmetic mean of $f$. For complete graphs, the optimal constant is known for $p\in[1,3+\delta_n^1)\cup(3+\delta_n^2,+\infty)$, with $\delta_n^1=\frac{1}{2n^2\ln n}+O(1/n^3)$ and $\delta_n^2=\frac{2}{n}+O(1/n^2)$. In this paper, we firstly extend the admissible range to all $p\in(0,\infty)$. Secondly, we obtain the sharp constant $C_{S_n,p}$ for the star graph $S_n$ in the range $p\in(0,+\infty)$ and give estimates for the sharp constant $C_{P_n,p}$ on path graphs when $p\in(0,+\infty)$. Thirdly, we characterize the extremizers on complete graphs and star graphs, and establish the existence of monotone extremizers on path graphs for $p\in(0,+\infty)$. For path graphs, we obtain explicit sharp constants for $p\in(0,1]\cup\{2\}$, and interpolation upper bounds for $p\in(1,+\infty)$. We also prove that for any finite connected graph $G_n$, the best constant at $p=+\infty$ is exactly its remoteness. Moreover, for general finite connected graphs $G_n$ and $p\in(0,+\infty)$, we establish optimal bounds for $C_{G_n,p}$; the complete graph uniquely attains the lower bound for all $p>0$; the path graph attains the upper bound for $p>1$, but for $0<p\leq1$ there exist nonpath graphs that attain the same supremum. Finally, we show that our approach yields sharper upper bounds than the path-based estimates obtained via the Cheeger constant.

papers.title: Normal and Unitary Operators on Smooth Banach Spaces via the Duality Mapping
papers.abstract: This article extends the classical notions of normal and unitary operators from Hilbert spaces to smooth Banach spaces through the duality mapping. The class of normal operators introduced in this setting contains, as a special case, the self-adjoint operators on smooth Banach spaces defined via the duality mapping. We establish several characterisations of these operators and investigate their fundamental properties. In particular, we examine various spectral properties of normal operators on smooth Banach spaces. These results demonstrate that many fundamental aspects of the classical theory of normal and unitary operators on Hilbert spaces persist in the smooth Banach space setting.

papers.title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
papers.abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_\Phi$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $\Delta_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

papers.title: The Descriptive Complexity of Continuous Selections with Prescribed Hausdorff dimension of the Graph
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of continuous selections of set-valued functions with prescribed Hausdorff dimension of their graphs. We consider Hausdorff-continuous functions defined on the unit interval whose values are nonempty compact subsets of the real line. We prove that, for every $\beta\in[1,2]$, the collection of all such functions admitting a continuous selection whose graph has Hausdorff dimension $\beta$ is $\Sigma^1_1$-complete and hence is not Borel. Further, we show that this result holds even when the set-valued functions have totally disconnected values. Thus, we obtain a complete classification of the descriptive complexity of the existence problem for all possible Hausdorff dimensions of continuous graphs over the unit interval.

papers.title: Kernel Estimates and Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund Theory in the $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre setting
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish heat and Poisson kernel estimates for $\mathfrak L=\|x\|^{2-a}\Delta_k$ in the $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre setting, where $\Delta_k$ is the Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group. The heat kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, and conservative, and satisfies a Gaussian bound in the orbit distance together with polynomial decay in the distance between the transformed coordinates. The Poisson kernel, obtained by subordination, satisfies corresponding size and time-derivative estimates, while $-t\partial_t p_t$ has integral zero in each variable. Motivated by these estimates, we introduce a class of $(k,a)$-Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund singular integral operators and show that $L^2_{k,a}$-boundedness implies $L^p_{k,a}$-boundedness for $1<p<\infty$, together with weak type $(1,1)$ and $L^\infty$-to-$\BMO$ estimates. Finally, we establish a $T1$ theorem characterizing the $L^2$-boundedness of such operators by the conditions $T1\in BMO$, $T^*1\in BMO$, and the weak boundedness property.

papers.title: Spontaneous Synchronization in Cellular Circadian Clocks
papers.abstract: We study a population of identical cellular circadian oscillators, each a four-species transcription--translation feedback loop of the type analysed by Wang and Peskin, coupled by the exchange of cytoplasmic mRNA with a shared, well-mixed bloodstream at rate $\epsilon$. Simulations started from uniformly random phases show a collective damping of the mean rhythm followed by spontaneous synchronization. We show that the blood compartment tracks the population mean on the time scale $1/[N_c(\epsilon+\delta_m)]$, and that the population means obey the single-cell equations with a correction proportional to the variance $\sigma_{pn}^2$ of nuclear protein across cells; the correction is accurate only near synchrony. Deviations from the mean obey a linear system with periodic coefficients, whose leading Floquet exponent $-\kappa(\epsilon)$ is the asymptotic synchronization rate. Using the fact that the four first-order stages of the feedback loop commute, we prove that $\kappa(\epsilon)=\epsilon/4+O(\epsilon^2)$ on the limit cycle in the large-population limit. Numerically computed exponents agree with the decay rates measured in simulations to within $0.2\%$ for $5$ to $400$ cells. The approach to synchrony from an incoherent state is slower than $\kappa$, and at the weakest coupling tested the population remains in a two-cluster state. With intrinsic molecular noise, uncoupled cells lose their autocorrelation within about ten cycles, whereas coupled cells retain it and sustain a Kuramoto order parameter of $0.68$ to $0.93$.

papers.title: Subnormality of $B$-operators of class $\mathscr{S}$
papers.abstract: We characterize subnormality of $B$-operators $T=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}V&E\\0&S\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ on $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\mathcal{H}_2$, where $V$ is an isometry, $V^*E=0$, $S$ is subnormal, and $S|E|=|E|S$. We determine when $T$ admits compactly supported signed elementary measures and express them explicitly in terms of the elementary measures of $S$. Requiring the signed elementary measures of $T$ to be positive yields a complete measure-theoretic characterization of the subnormality of $T$. If $E$ is injective, $T$ is subnormal if and only if it is a contraction. In the general case, the subnormality of $T$ is equivalent to the contractivity of its restriction to $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\overline{{\mathcal R}(|E|)}$. We also obtain equivalent criteria involving the Taylor spectra of $(S,|E|)$, its minimal normal and minimal quasinormal extensions, and the corresponding pairs of moduli. These results extend the characterization previously known for a quasinormal lower-right entry.

papers.title: Finite rank and compactness of finite sums of Toeplitz products on the harmonic Bergman space
papers.abstract: We completely characterize finite rank and compactness for finite sums of products of Toeplitz operators on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk, assuming boundedness only of the full harmonic symbols. Reflecting the appropriate symbols reduces sums of Toeplitz products and small Hankel products to Toeplitz product sums. For sums of mixed Toeplitz and small Hankel products in either order, right multiplication by a fixed unitary reflection gives the corresponding reduction. These reductions preserve rank and compactness. Finite rank is characterized by symbol identities and a cubic divisibility condition on the coefficient polynomials obtained after choosing bases over one-variable rational function fields. We also obtain an exact rank formula. Compactness is characterized by boundary vanishing of the diagonal symbol sum and uniform decay of the centered symbol tensor on hyperbolic disks of fixed radius as their centers approach the boundary. For a sum of $N\ge1$ products, an equivalent compactness criterion uses weighted derivatives of the symbol components up to order $N$. When $N$ is even, the conditions of order $N$ cannot be omitted. Mixed commutators of finite rank vanish. We characterize small Hankel commutators of nonzero finite rank in terms of a bounded analytic function and its bounded reciprocal, both with rational primitives.

papers.title: Ranges of vector measures and copies of $c_0$
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space such that every weakly compact subset of $X$ is contained in the range of an $X$-valued countably additive vector measure defined on a $\sigma$-algebra. We prove that $X$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$, thereby answering a question posed by R. Anantharaman and J. Diestel [Comment. Math. Prace Mat. 30 (1991), no. 2, 221--235]. In particular, every Banach lattice with this property is superreflexive.

papers.title: Partial Self-Similar Fractal Interpolation Functions and Surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of fractal interpolation functions with partial self-similarity. We first study fractal interpolation surfaces defined on rectangular domains, analyze the stability and sensitivity of the proposed construction to parameter perturbations. In addition, we investigate the partial $\alpha$-fractal function in both the univariate and bivariate cases, as well as the invariant measure in the univariate setting whose support is the graph of the fractal interpolation function. Further, under suitable additional conditions, we derive bounds for the box-counting dimension of the graph of the univariate PFIF. The results presented in this paper are backed up by illustrative examples.

papers.title: Taylor invertibility and the completion problem for commuting tuples of upper triangular operator matrices
papers.abstract: We study commuting $n$-tuples of upper triangular operator matrices $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} \mathbf{A} & \mathbf{C} \\ \mathbf{0} & \mathbf{B} \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ acting on a direct sum of Banach spaces. Using the long exact sequence in cohomology induced by the Koszul complexes, we show that $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}}$ is Taylor invertible if and only if the connecting homomorphisms $H^k(\mathbf{B}) \to H^{k+1}(\mathbf{A})$ are linear bijections in every degree, and that under natural closed-range hypotheses on the diagonal tuples these bijections are automatically topological isomorphisms. We determine which closed-range properties of the diagonal tuples are forced by the Taylor invertibility of $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}}$ and show by an example that the remaining ones fail in general. We then study the multivariable invertible completion problem, that is, the existence of a coupling tuple $\mathbf{C}$ for which $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}}$ is Taylor invertible. We reduce it to the realization of a family of cohomological isomorphisms by a single coupling tuple, show that the cohomology of $\mathbf{B}$ and the shifted cohomology of $\mathbf{A}$ must be isomorphic as graded modules over the exterior algebra, and exhibit diagonal tuples whose cohomology spaces are topologically isomorphic in every degree but which admit no Taylor invertible completion, a phenomenon with no one-dimensional counterpart.

papers.title: Polar Carleson zeto set preventing Dirichlet cyclicity
papers.abstract: The work of Chen, Fang and Guo shows, finally, that the Brown-Shields conjecture is false. In this note, we construct a polar Carleson set E on the unit circle T which has the property that any H\"older continuous function in the Dirichlet space vanishing on E is non-cyclic.

papers.title: The Commutant of the Adjoint Center Need Not Be the Center of the Dual
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach lattice with ideal center $Z(X)$, and let $Z^*(X)=\{S^*:S\in Z(X)\}$ be the set of adjoints of central operators, acting on the dual $X^*$. The center $Z(X^*)$ of the dual is always contained in the commutant $(Z^*(X))^{\mathrm{com}}$ of $Z^*(X)$, and equality is known when $X$ has a topological order unit. It has been asserted that equality holds whenever $X$ has a topologically full center; the published proof of this assertion is incorrect, and the question has been recorded as open. We show that the assertion is false. For the Marcinkiewicz sequence space $m_\psi$, $\psi(t)=\log(1+t)$ (the sequence space underlying the Dixmier--Macaev ideal), which is Dedekind complete and therefore has a topologically full center, there is a bounded operator on the dual that commutes with every adjoint of a central operator but is not itself central; it maps one Dixmier trace onto another one disjoint from it. The construction rests on a general sufficient condition, proved with an invariant mean taking values in a Dedekind complete space $C(K)$ and the injectivity of $C(K)$. We also collect positive results and a norm-density criterion for equality. For every Orlicz space $L_\Phi$ we show that every operator in $(Z^*(L_\Phi))^{\mathrm{com}}$ is lower-triangular with respect to the decomposition of the dual into its order continuous and singular bands, with central diagonal entries, and, by a splitting lemma based on Young's inequality, that the off-diagonal entry vanishes. Hence equality holds for all Orlicz spaces and their duals, without any $\Delta_2$-condition.

papers.title: A note on slicing
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of Bourgain's slicing theorem with the explicit bound $L_K\leq\sqrt{5/\pi}$ for every convex body $K$. The argument combines the strong thin-shell inequality obtained from the moment-measure method of Chen and Klartag with an entropy estimate along Eldan's stochastic localization. The proof uses neither $M$-ellipsoid theory nor the reverse Santal\'o inequality.

papers.title: A characterization of almost everywhere convergence of subsequences of Walsh--Fourier partial sums
papers.abstract:
We characterize the increasing sequences $(
u_j)$ in the set of positive integers $\mathbb N$ along which the Walsh--Fourier partial sums $s_{
u_j}(f)$ of every integrable function $f$ converge almost everywhere to $f$. This resolves a problem that Konyagin posed in his invited address at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians~\cite{K06}. The criterion concerns the binary expansions of the integers $
u_j$. Divide each $
u_j$ by $2^k$. Convergence holds if and only if, for some $K\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct positive quotients whose remainder has binary variation larger than $K$ is bounded independently of the scale $k$. This is also equivalent to the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for $\sup_{j\in\mathbb N}|s_{
u_j}(f)|$, and if the criterion fails, then the partial sums of some integrable function along $(
u_j)$ are unbounded at every point. The criterion contains the bounded variation condition and Konyagin's condition for separated spectra, and we give examples, for convergence and for divergence, that are not covered by the earlier results.

papers.title: Bounded N\"orlund operators on Hardy spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize the nonnegative N\"orlund matrices that induce bounded operators on Hardy spaces. For $a_n\ge0$ and $a_0>0$, boundedness on one $H^p$, $1<p<\infty$, is equivalent to boundedness on every such space and to a single quadratic testing condition involving the ratios of the partial sums $A_n=\sum_{k=0}^na_k$. The testing constant is comparable to the squared $H^2$ operator norm, with absolute constants. No doubling or monotonicity assumption on the weights is required. The proof combines an exact vector-valued Hankel representation with square-function estimates and a geometric argument showing that the doubling-time endpoints have finite lacunary order. Equivalently, boundedness is characterized by a truncated quadratic block condition on the coefficients of $G_a(z)=\sum_n(a_n/A_n)z^n$. Within the bounded family, $G_a$ belongs to the Bloch space if and only if it belongs to $BMOA$, and this occurs exactly when $(A_n)$ is doubling.

papers.title: Rank 1 composition factors in the polydisk
papers.abstract: For an isometry-invariant reproducing kernel $k$ on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{D}^d$, we consider its composition factors, analytic selfmaps $\phi:\mathbb{D}^d\to\mathbb{D}^d$ such that $k^\phi=k/(k\circ\phi)$ is a reproducing kernel. Denoting its corresponding Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}(k^\phi)$, we define the rank of $\phi$ with respect to $k$ as the dimension of $\mathcal{H}(k^\phi)$. Using these notions, we reframe recent work considering co-isometric weighted composition operators in the unit disk by Mas, Mart\'in, and Vukoti\'c, and in the unit ball by Hartz and Tornes. That is, we illustrate a bijective correspondence between the above operators and rank $1$ composition operators, and extend their results to the setting of the polydisk. Namely, supposing that $\phi$ is a rank $1$ composition factor of $k$ and assuming that $k$ is either bounded or unbounded everywhere on $\partial\mathbb{D}^d$, we prove that $\phi$ must be an automorphism. Moreover, if it is not a composition of a rotation and permutation, then $k$ must be a positive power of the Szeg\H{o} kernel. We also briefly consider finite rank composition factors.

papers.title: Disjointness, Orthogonality and Commutativity in $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: We characterize order-theoretic disjointness of two elements $a$ and $b$ in the self-adjoint part of a $C^*$-algebra $A$ via the condition $aAb = \{0\}$ and the trivial intersection of closed two-sided ideals generated by $a$ and $b$. As a consequence, we show that disjoint complements coincide with the self-adjoint parts of annihilator ideals. We also prove that $A$ is commutative whenever every pair of algebraically orthogonal positive contractions in $A$ is disjoint. Finally, we establish corresponding commutativity criteria involving projections for real rank zero $C^*$-algebras.
